name: Zoko
tagline: A Y Combinator-backed WhatsApp commerce platform built by founders who ran their own WhatsApp-only ecommerce business first — and one of the best-reviewed tools in this entire category.
tldr: Zoko was founded in 2021 in Bengaluru by Arjun Paul and Aromal Sivadasan, who built the product after running their own successful ecommerce business entirely on WhatsApp — a genuinely authentic founder-market-fit story rather than a generic pivot into the space.

Company funding is a bit unclear from public sources: some describe Zoko as built with no outside investment, while others cite $1.4-1.56M raised from Y Combinator, Flipkart co-founder Binny Bansal's family office, and angel investors — likely reflecting a largely self-sufficient business that took some early seed capital rather than a fully bootstrapped one.

Pricing is unusually precise and transparent: Starter $49.99/mo (unlimited agents, $0.015/conversation), Plus $79.99/mo (5 agents, no per-conversation fee, 100K conversation fair-use cap), Elite $139.99/mo (10 agents, 1M cap), Max $499.99/mo (30 agents, 5M cap) — plus itemized add-ons like the $4.99/mo Shopify plugin and $9.99/mo Instagram channel.

The Shopify integration is genuinely exceptional: automatic catalog sync lets customers browse and place orders directly inside WhatsApp, with automated abandoned-cart recovery and order-update messaging built around real commerce workflows.

Review sentiment is outstanding and unusually consistent — 4.9/5 across 382 Shopify App Store reviews — with reviewers specifically praising the seamless Shopify integration, system stability, and a responsive support team that understands both technical and business requirements.

The AI chatbot capability is real but modestly scoped — ChatGPT-powered bots for FAQs and simple conversation flows — genuinely less sophisticated than some competitors' more agentic implementations, though the product doesn't need to oversell this since its commerce workflow depth carries the value proposition.
keyFeatures: Automatic Shopify product catalog sync, letting customers browse and place orders directly inside WhatsApp
WhatsApp-based abandoned-cart recovery with automated reminders and checkout completion inside the chat
ChatGPT-powered chatbots handling FAQs, order collection, and simple conversation flows

A multi-agent shared inbox for teams managing WhatsApp and Instagram conversations together
Customer segmentation for targeted broadcast campaigns and marketing automation
Custom automation flows, billed per-flow ($5.99/month each) for businesses needing bespoke conversation logic
Shopify App Store presence with a large, verified, consistently positive review base

faq.question: Is Zoko's founding story really from running their own WhatsApp store?
faq.answer: Yes — this is a genuinely distinctive origin story in this category. Co-founders Arjun Paul and Aromal Sivadasan built Zoko after first running their own successful ecommerce business entirely on WhatsApp, which means the product's commerce-first design (catalog sync, in-chat checkout, cart recovery) reflects lived operational experience rather than a generic feature checklist built to compete in a category.

faq.question: How good is Zoko's Shopify integration specifically?
faq.answer: It's the clearest strength of the whole product. Product catalogs sync automatically so customers can browse and order directly inside WhatsApp, abandoned carts trigger automated recovery messages with in-chat checkout completion, and order confirmations and shipping updates fire automatically off Shopify events. Independent reviewers consistently and specifically name this integration, alongside system stability, as the reason they chose Zoko.

faq.question: How sophisticated is Zoko's AI chatbot?
faq.answer: Genuinely more modest than some AI-forward competitors — it's described as basic ChatGPT-powered bots for FAQs and simple conversation flows, rather than a deeply agentic system with multi-step actions or CRM lifecycle management. This isn't necessarily a weakness for Zoko's target buyer, since the product's real value proposition is commerce-workflow depth rather than AI sophistication, but don't expect Interakt- or Wati-level dedicated commerce-AI agents specifically.

faq.question: How much does Zoko actually cost?
faq.answer: Starting at $49.99/month for the Starter plan (unlimited agents, $0.015 per conversation), rising to $79.99, $139.99, and $499.99/month for higher tiers that trade the per-conversation fee for a flat monthly rate with a generous conversation cap. Add-ons are itemized clearly: the Shopify plugin is $4.99/month, Instagram is $9.99/month, and custom automation flows run $5.99/month each — genuinely one of the more transparently, precisely published pricing pages in this category.

faq.question: Does Zoko support channels beyond WhatsApp?
faq.answer: Instagram is available as a documented add-on ($9.99/month), but this remains a narrower channel scope than broader omnichannel competitors like Respond.io or Trengo. If your business genuinely centers on WhatsApp commerce specifically, this focus works in Zoko's favor; if you need broader channel coverage, look elsewhere.

faq.question: How does Zoko compare to Wati or Interakt?
faq.answer: All three are India-origin, Shopify-focused WhatsApp commerce tools, but Zoko's review sentiment is notably stronger and more consistent (4.9/5 across 382 reviews) than either, without the serious billing complaints documented for Wati or the dated review base found for Interakt. Zoko's AI chatbot is more modestly scoped than Wati's multi-layered AI stack, so the tradeoff is real commerce-workflow reliability and review consistency versus more ambitious (but less independently verified) AI capability.

pricingBreakdown: Zoko's pricing is unusually easy to model precisely compared to most competitors in this category — every tier price, every add-on cost, and the exact per-conversation fee structure are published clearly rather than requiring a sales conversation to piece together. The Starter tier's $0.015-per-conversation fee disappears entirely on Plus and above, replaced by a generous fair-use conversation cap (100K on Plus, scaling to 5M on Max) — a genuinely sensible structure that rewards committing to a higher tier once your volume justifies it. Itemized add-ons (Shopify plugin at $4.99/month, Instagram at $9.99/month, custom flows at $5.99/month each) keep the total cost calculable rather than opaque. The one variable genuinely outside Zoko's control is Meta's own WhatsApp messaging costs, which shifted from per-24-hour-conversation to per-message billing on January 1, 2026 — factor that platform-level change into your cost model regardless of which Zoko tier you choose.

capabilities.note: This is Zoko's entire reason for existing, built by founders who ran their own WhatsApp store first, and it shows in genuinely thoughtful execution: automatic catalog sync, in-chat ordering, and abandoned-cart recovery that completes checkout without leaving WhatsApp. Independent reviewers consistently and specifically name this as the reason they chose the platform, and the 4.9/5 review average across 382 reviews backs that up.

Real but appropriately modest — ChatGPT-powered bots handle FAQs and simple conversation flows well, without overpromising the kind of dedicated, multi-step agentic capability some competitors market more aggressively. For a Shopify-first business whose priority is reliable commerce automation rather than sophisticated AI, this scoping is honest rather than a limitation.

Deliberately narrow: WhatsApp plus an Instagram add-on. This focus is a feature, not a bug, for the specific buyer Zoko targets — a Shopify DTC brand running its customer relationship primarily through WhatsApp — but it's a real constraint if your business needs broader channel coverage.

One of the strongest, most consistent independent review records found in this entire category — 4.9/5 across 382 Shopify App Store reviews is a genuinely large, genuinely positive sample, with support responsiveness and system stability specifically and repeatedly named rather than generic praise.

A real, honest gap worth noting: no confirmed native CRM integration beyond Zoko's own built-in system, no website-builder integrations, and no documented multi-language or advanced analytics capability. This is a focused tool, not a broad platform, and buyers should evaluate it on that basis rather than expecting enterprise-platform breadth.

verdict: Zoko is a genuinely well-executed example of a narrowly-scoped product done right, and its origin story is the reason why: founders who built and ran their own WhatsApp ecommerce business before building this platform for others tend to get the actual workflow details correct in a way a generic pivot into the space often doesn't. That shows up directly in the Shopify integration, which is the clear standout of the entire product — automatic catalog sync, in-chat ordering, and abandoned-cart recovery that completes checkout without ever leaving WhatsApp, backed by one of the strongest and most consistent independent review records in this whole category (4.9/5 across 382 reviews, with support responsiveness specifically and repeatedly praised rather than generically mentioned). The AI chatbot capability is honestly more modest than some competitors' — ChatGPT-powered bots for FAQs and simple flows, not a deeply agentic, multi-step system — but that's a reasonable scoping choice for a product whose real value is commerce-workflow reliability rather than AI sophistication, and it doesn't oversell what it offers. The pricing is refreshingly precise and easy to model, a genuine point in its favor against competitors that require a sales call to understand real costs. My honest read: if you're a Shopify-first DTC brand running your customer relationship through WhatsApp and want a reliable, well-reviewed, and transparently priced tool for it, Zoko is one of the stronger picks in this category. If you need broader channel coverage, deep CRM integration, or more ambitious AI capability, look at Respond.io, Trengo, or Wati instead — all reviewed elsewhere on this site — with the tradeoff that none of them match Zoko's review consistency on the specific job it's built for.
